reasons.problem: [source] sec1 for the hardness ('finding an optimal decomposition is believed to be very hard') and for prior low success ('only with some probability that rapidly fell to zero as the number of qubits grew'). The 'respond by heavily overparameterizing' clause comes from the STORED abstract, not the body -- see the report's coverage note; it is faithful to what the curator was shown even though arXiv's current abstract lacks it.
reasons.setting: [source] almost entirely verbatim: 'a circuit of depth Theta(4^n/n) is required, as given by parameter counting' (sec1); 'the CNOT gate is the unique two-qubit entangling gate, and arbitrary single-qubit unitaries are allowed' (sec3.1); '1D or star-topology qubit layouts' (sec1, realised in App. C.2 and C.1); trace-distance cost (sec3.2); 'Our investigations are empirical' and 'never failed even across hundreds of trials' (sec1), with sec4.2 giving ~330 runs. NOTE: the marks that were cleared had this at p. I cannot locate the defect -- if you had a reason it is worth more than the verdict.
reasons.method: [source] sec1 for skeleton-plus-parameter-search and for GRAPE ('gradient descent-based approaches, sometimes referred to as GRAPE'); sec3.1 for the skeleton definition and for 'this random search is unnecessary, and we can simply pick an ideal skeleton from the get-go using a simple design principle'; sec1 + sec4.1 for the underparameterization mechanism ('The surplus parameters introduce redundancies in the circuit, leading to symmetries'). Omission not scored: the prescription is 1-factorization of a k-node graph (sec4.1), a named object the card gestures at as 'a prescription'.
reasons.contribution: [source] sec1 near-verbatim for the three optimality claims: 'These circuits naturally turn out to be optimal in terms of the number of entangling gates, and in the number of total gates, as well.' 1D/star from sec1. The diagnosis half is the abstract, and Appendix D quantifies it against the prior work's own reported numbers ('This agrees very well with the numbers reported in [3]').
reasons.limitations: [source] bullets 1, 2, 4 hold -- bullet 1 quotes 'our investigations are empirical' correctly and rightly notes the no-local-minima claim is a CONJECTURE; bullet 2 matches sec4.2's 2/4/6-qubit range. BULLET 3 IS OVERSTATED: 'no general criterion is given for when a skeleton is parameter-deficient'. Appendix D gives one -- compute the topology's effective parameter count, and if it is below 4^n-1 failure is generically necessary -- applied in closed form for n=3 and by program for n=4,5, matching prior work's measured failure rates. open_questions bullet 2 compounds it by posing as open a question Appendix D substantially answers. SAME SHAPE as 2608.17381's BoltzDesign bullet: an absence asserted from sections that could not contain the evidence (sections_read is [abstract, intro, conclusion]). Bullet 5 mildly overstated too -- sec3.2.2 works out parameter loss for CZ, Sycamore, generic two-qubit and SWAP.

Unitary synthesis.reason: [source] Object and role right (sec1 opens by defining it). ALIAS CONTRADICTED BY THE PAPER: 'unitary compilation' is listed as a synonym, but sec2 separates them deliberately -- 'When the unitary is already given as a circuit... this process is typically referred to as compiling. Meanwhile, synthesis typically refers to when the unitary is given as the full 2^n x 2^n matrix.' Different input, different problem, and sec2 spends a paragraph on why compilers are not parameter-optimal, which is half the motivation. Merges two nodes the source separates on purpose. Consistent with 2606.07914's 'mixing matrix' and 2608.17381's 'trust region'. NOTE: the cleared marks had this at y.

Non-convex optimization landscape.reason: [source] sec1 'The resulting optimization problem is highly non-convex' and 'we conjecture that the resulting loss landscape has no local minima'. Role's claim that the landscape is benign exactly when the skeleton is not parameter-deficient is that conjecture plus sec1's 'gradient descent fails only when certain bad circuit skeletons are selected'.

Gradient descent.reason: [source] sec1 'gradient descent-based approaches, sometimes referred to as GRAPE' -- the alias is the paper's own word. Role accurate: sec1 'gradient descent is able to find a depth-optimal circuit every time' and sec3.1 on replacing random search.

Overparameterization.reason: [source] the stored abstract ('heavily overparameterized circuits') and Appendix B ('we look at circuits that are slightly over-parameterized'). Role is accurate and survives App. B's twist -- overparameterized circuits do converge FASTER, but the paper's claim is that overparameterization is unnecessary, not useless, which is exactly what the role says.

Parameter counting.reason: [source] sec1 'as given by parameter counting' verbatim; sec3.2.2 'This is a straightforward exercise in parameter counting', deriving eq (7) l = ceil((4^n-1-n)/2n). Role correctly ties it to both the depth bound and the meaning of 'parameter-deficient'.

Circuit skeleton / ansatz topology.reason: [source] sec3.1 'The pattern of CNOTs dictates what we call the circuit skeleton', held constant during gradient descent. Role accurate incl. the layer-symmetry point (sec4.1). NAME IS COMPOUND -- third slash-or-parenthesis name in five cards after 'Hermitization (Girko's method)' and 'Subset-rank and no-cancellation conditions'. Validator candidate: reject a name containing '/', '(' or ' and '.

Hardware connectivity constraints.reason: [source] sec4.3 'practical quantum hardware typically imposes connectivity constraints that limit the combination of qubits that can be directly entangled'; Appendix C realises both cases on sub-systems of the 127-qubit IBM chip. Role accurate.

notes:
FULL-TEXT REVIEW including Appendices A-D. Four of five prose fields clean, one object defect, three missed objects.

STORED-ABSTRACT ANOMALY, and this is the strangest of three. papers.sqlite holds a LONGER abstract containing 'Previous approaches based on random combinatorial search indicate a low success rate... motivating the use of heavily overparameterized circuits' and 'We prescribe parameter-optimal circuit skeletons'. Neither sentence appears on the arXiv abs page or in the v1 HTML, both of which carry a shorter rewrite. On the two previous cards the DB held text arXiv had revised AWAY; here it holds text present in no version I can reach, and it is MORE detailed than what arXiv shows. The card's problem field is built on that sentence -- judged against arXiv it looks unsupported, judged against what the curator was shown it is faithful. Three of four cards now show this drift, and this is the cleanest demonstration that checking a card against live arXiv can manufacture a false fabrication finding, which is precisely the error I made on 2606.07914. Worth establishing whether a v2 exists; it bears on all 28 cards.

OBJECT DEFECT: 'Unitary synthesis' aliases 'unitary compilation', which sec2 explicitly separates -- compiling takes a circuit, synthesis takes the full 2^n x 2^n matrix -- and the paper spends a paragraph on why compilers are not parameter-optimal, which is half its motivation. The card merges two nodes the source distinguishes on purpose.

LIMITATIONS DEFECT, second occurrence of a shape now seen in cards as well as in my own drafts: bullet 3 says no general criterion exists for identifying parameter-deficient skeletons, and open_questions bullet 2 poses it as open. Appendix D gives a computable criterion (effective parameter count below 4^n-1 implies generic failure), works it in closed form for n=3 and by program for n=4,5, and matches the prior work's measured failure rates. An absence asserted from sections that could not contain the evidence.

THE MISSING-OBJECT PATTERN NOW HAS A VISIBLE CAUSE. Fifth card running with load-bearing concepts absent from the object list -- and here all three missed objects (1-factorization, trace distance, Haar measure) live in sec3 or sec4, while sections_read is [abstract, intro, conclusion]. A curator reading only abstract/intro/conclusion STRUCTURALLY CANNOT list objects introduced in the methodology and results, because that is where the machinery is defined. Pair this with 2606.07914, the one card where the extractor DID catch the conclusion and whose limitations were correspondingly sharper: the missing-object pattern and the weak-limitations pattern are one finding, and it is EXTRACTION COVERAGE, upstream of the curator. That changes the fix from a prompt edit to pdf_extract.py's section matching.

ROUTING, not a card defect: this is a quantum-computing paper in kb/compbio_methods/, as is 2509.18530. The card's own cross_domain_note flags moderate charter fit, so the curator noticed. Belongs in OPEN-QUESTIONS.
